description: Iteration 2: same structure as the best it01 spec (s01), with faster discharge (lower tau/sigma), much stronger early start and red running (it01 gave 0.02 and 0.006 shares against 0.13 and 0.098 observed), fewer sidewalk riders, lane-change gain to spread straight vehicles out of lane 0, and the box-waiter parameters of it01_s02, which matched M7b.

driver_archetypes.rationale: Targets M1/car (sim 0.50-0.63 s vs obs 0.347 s) and the queue length M5/length (38-44 m vs 15.8 m): lower tau, sigma and minGap and higher accel shorten the discharge headway and the queue (it01_s03 with tau 0.9/sigma 0.4 was already closest); lcSpeedGain 3 lets cars leave the lane-0 queue for faster lanes, targeting M9a/M9b (17 straight vehicles/cycle in the right-turn lane vs 0.57 obs).

Targets M1/moto (sim 0.38-0.48 s vs obs 0.296 s) with a smaller tau and sigma (it01_s03 style, defaults for accel/decel kept since they scored better than accel 4); minGap 1.0 m with compact lateral packing targets M5/moto_density (0.097-0.099 vs 0.052 veh/m2, too dense); lcSpeedGain 3 spreads riders out of lane 0 for M9a/M9b.

Targets M6/approach s/moto (sim 38-46 s vs obs 35.7 s): the 0.10 share and speedFactor 0.8 keep the slow lane-centre riders as a minority so approach times do not rise further above the observed means.
Targets M10a/per_cycle (sim 1.7-3.6 vs obs 0.56 sidewalk riders/cycle): the seeker share goes from 0.25-0.30 to 0.15, with the same filtering parameters as moto_std so the other metrics do not move.

Targets M7a/M7b: these are the it01_s02 values (no impatience), which gave the best box result (M7b/clear_lag 5.453 vs 5.459 s, M7a/n_waiting 4.3 vs 5.6) while impatience 0.3-0.5 in s01/s03 made waiters leave early (n_waiting 1.6-1.9, negative release_time); kept unchanged.

traci_rules.rationale: Targets M2/early/moto (sim 0.017-0.024 vs obs 0.130) and M4/overshoot_share (sim 0 vs obs 0.62): p 0.13-0.15 gave about one seventh of p as an observed share, so p is raised to 0.7 and the window to the full 10 s so front-row riders creep over the stop line; v_max 2.0 kept since it01_s02 had the best M2/first_delay (1.18 s vs 2.83).
Targets M2/early/car (sim 0.001-0.005 vs obs 0.0111): by the same one-seventh scaling p 0.07 gives about 0.01 and cars stay almost compliant.

Targets M3/share/moto (sim 0.005-0.007 vs obs 0.098) and M3/per_cycle (0.2-0.3 vs 3.9): p0 0.06 produced about a tenth of p0 as a share, so p0 0.5 (the front-row value of Saval et al. 2023 given in the dictionary) with k 0.1 raises it to the observed order; var/mean was already near 1.14 and the modest k keeps the clustering.
Targets M3/share/car (sim 0 vs obs 0.0041): by the same one-tenth scaling p0 0.04 gives about 0.004 with no swarm effect, so cars stay almost compliant.

Targets M10a/per_cycle (sim 1.7-3.6 vs obs 0.56) and M10b/queue_at_choice (sim 43-56 m vs obs 15.3 m): p_sidewalk is lowered from 0.05-0.1 to 0.03 and the trigger q raised to 15 m, near the observed choice queue 15.3 m, so riders only seek space in short queues; p_wrong_lane stays at 0.3 as in it01_s02 and p_right_lane is 0 because the option does not exist on this site.
Targets M7a/release_time (sim 3.7 vs obs 2.78 s) and M7b/clear_lag (5.453 vs 5.459 s): 1.0 s is the it01_s02 value that matched the clear lag, so it is not changed to avoid fitting noise.
Targets M6/approach moto times (behaviour 10): slow riders keep the lane centre (offset 0); no measured offset is available, so the base value is kept.
